**Verdict:** Kill the checklist; weaponize incumbent breadth as tax, force stopwatch evals over spreadsheets.

1. **Reframe bloat as liability:** Turn their feature count into maintenance drag, config hell, shelfware, mandatory consultants. Pitch: *"Pay for 100 features, use 6, maintain 100."*
2. **Shift eval from breadth to velocity:** Refuse static feature matrices. Demand timed POCs on 2–3 daily workflows (cold-start setup, config LOC, onboarding hrs). Incumbents win spreadsheets, lose stopwatches.
3. **Anchor on architecture, not parity:** Never sell "Incumbent Lite." Own a shift their legacy core can't retrofit (e.g., zero-config, local-first, code-native, AI-native) so their checkboxes read like legacy baggage.
4. **Plant demo landmines:** Arm internal champions w/ trap questions for the incumbent (*"Demo setup from scratch in <15 min w/o an SE," "Quote TCO incl. dedicated admin headcount & upgrade downtime"*).
5. **Wedge via greenfield, skip rip-and-replace:** Enterprise checklists exist to price migration risk. Position to co-exist alongside the incumbent on net-new projects; expand once ICs refuse to go back.
6. **Disqualify CYA buyers early:** If procurement owns the rubric & devs have no veto, walk—feature checklists are cover-your-ass mechanisms built to rubber-stamp the incumbent.
